s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, cutaneous vascular lesions with erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
salient_findings: Multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
Firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders
Thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels dispersed between thickened collagen bundles
key_facts: Female patient in her late 20s
2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions located on left upper arm, left axilla, and lateral thoracic region
No triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma occurred before lesion appearance
No fever, weight loss, or fatigue
No extracutaneous involvement observed
Histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels
Endothelial cells were plump but displayed no significant cytologic atypia
Immunohistochemistry results positive for CD31, CD34, Ki-67 (<1%)
Immunohistochemistry results negative for podoplanin (D2-40), human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)

shortlist.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, and histopathological findings of irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels

shortlist.label: Tufted angioma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the patient's skin lesions and histopathological examination showing irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels

shortlist.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible match given the patient's presentation of erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, and the presence of plump endothelial cells on histopathology

shortlist.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the patient's clinical presentation and histopathological findings, although less common than other options

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely due to the absence of HHV-8 positivity, it remains a consideration given the patient's skin lesions and histopathological examination results

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, along with the histopathological findings of irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels and plump endothelial cells, is consistent with Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma. The immunohistochemistry results, including positivity for CD31 and CD34, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Tufted angioma
rejected.why: Tufted angiomas typically present with a more localized and nodular appearance, which does not match the patient's widespread and infiltrative lesions.

rejected.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
rejected.why: Epithelioid hemangiomas are characterized by a distinct epithelioid morphology of endothelial cells, which was not described in the patient's histopathological examination.

rejected.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Retiform hemangioendotheliomas typically exhibit a retiform (net-like) vascular pattern, which was not observed in the patient's histopathological examination.

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Kaposi's sarcoma is typically associated with human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) infection, which was negative in the patient's immunohistochemistry results.
